doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: No wrong notes, only wrong lines
summary: Longo explains resolving non-harmonic tones so no note is wrong.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Do you think that he thought there was no such things as wrong notes in improvising. I’m not sure I asked that very well, but the idea that there are wrong notes when you improvise, I wonder if —

I’ll say it this way. There are no wrong notes but there are wrong lines. And so relief is a half step away. And so Dizzy and Miles and those cats, they were masters of non- harmonic tones with the proper resolutions. Because the whole chromatic scale can be related to one triad if you resolve everything properly. And so if you land wrong, man, you could make it an appoggiatura, a step up into the chord. And so Dizzy, he was a master at it. So was Charlie Parker. So there are only wrong notes if you play the wrong notes. But there is no such thing as a wrong note that doesn’t fit the harmonic situation you’re in, if you know how to resolve it properly. So yeah, you could play wrong notes. They sound terrible you know. But it’s not the note, it’s you.
